Opc.Ua.SpecificationPublisher — build an OPC UA companion specification from markdown.

  build [--manifest spec.json] [--out _work/artifacts]
        markdown + NodeSet -> NISO STS 1.2 Extended XML

  publish [--in _work/artifacts] [--out _work/docs]
        STS -> the browsable specification. One HTML page:
        numbered clauses, real tables, figures, and every
        cross-reference resolved. That is the artifact an author
        reviews - the markdown source carries no numbering and the
        STS is not for reading.

        Renders the XML rather than the document the build had in
        memory, on purpose. The STS is what every downstream
        rendering comes from, so reading it back makes the page a
        standing check on it: whatever the STS failed to carry is
        visibly missing here.

        The output directory is served as-is, so it is what Pages
        publishes from a branch folder - point Pages at main /docs.

Both verbs write under _work/ by default, which is gitignored: a local
build is run to look at the result, and rebuilding should not leave the
committed artifacts dirty. The workflow names artifacts/ and docs/
explicitly, so what gets committed is decided in the workflow rather
than by where the command happens to be running.

  fetch-dependencies [--cloud-lib-user <name>]
        Download the NodeSets this model requires into
        model/dependencies/ so they can be committed. Run locally; a
        build never reaches the network, and a missing dependency is a
        validation error.

  update-tables [--write]
        Bring the markdown into line with the model. Reports by default;
        --write applies, and you read the diff.

          * renames table and figure anchors to the convention and
            updates every reference to them, so an author can write
            {#t1} and cite [](#t1) rather than typing the long form;
          * reports every citation with no target — an anchor this
            document does not declare, or a #ref- that spec.json does
  
[truncated]
